title: Money
seo_title: Money maths practice: pounds, pence, change and budgets (KS2)
description: Practise money maths with UK coins and notes: pounds and pence, adding prices, working out change, multiplying and sharing money, best buys and simple budgets. Free questions with hints for ages 9 to 11.
intro: Shopping, pocket money and saving up: money maths is maths you use every day. Learn to add prices, work out change and find the best deal.

units.title: Pounds and pence
units.blurb: Coins, notes, and writing amounts with a decimal point.

learn.p: There are 100 pence in £1. So 350p is £3.50: 3 whole pounds and 50 pence. The decimal point separates the pounds from the pence.
We write pence with two digits after the point. 5 pounds and 7 pence is £5.07, not £5.7. (£5.7 would mean £5.70, which is 5 pounds 70 pence.)

questions.q: How much money is shown, in pence?
questions.hint: Add up from the biggest coin.

questions.q: How much money is shown, in pounds? Type it like 3.50
questions.hint: Add the pounds, then the pence.

questions.q: Write 245p in pounds.
questions.hint: 100p = £1. How many whole hundreds are in 245?

questions.q: How many pence is £4.08?
How do you write 6 pounds and 5 pence?
questions.hint: Pence always use two digits after the point.
questions.explain: 5 pence is written 05 after the point: £6.05.

questions.q: How many 20p coins make £1?
A comic costs £2.30 and a drink costs £1.45. What is the total in pounds?
Three apples cost 35p each. How much is that in pence?
A pen costs £0.99 and a notebook costs £2.99. What is the total in pounds?

questions.hint: Look for pence that add up to 100, like 75p and 25p.

units.title: Giving change
units.blurb: Count on from the price to the money you paid.

learn.p: You buy a toy for £3.60 and pay with a £5 note. Count on from £3.60: 40p takes you to £4, then £1 takes you to £5. Change: £1.40.
You can also work out £5.00 − £3.60 = £1.40. Counting on is often easier in your head, and it's how shop assistants used to count change into your hand.
Price + change should equal the money you paid: £3.60 + £1.40 = £5.00. ✔

questions.q: You buy a drink for 65p and pay with £1. How much change do you get?
A book costs £4.20. You pay with a £5 note. How much change in pence?
A T-shirt costs £7.35. You pay with £10. How much change in pounds?
You spend £13.50 and pay with a £20 note. How much change in pounds?
Two cinema snacks cost £2.45 each. You pay with £5. How much change in pence?
Ben buys a game for £8.75 and pays with £10. He gets £2.25 change. Is that right?
questions.explain: £8.75 + £2.25 = £11, too much. Count on: 25p to £9, then £1 to £10. Change £1.25.

units.title: Multiplying and sharing money
units.blurb: Several of the same item, or splitting a bill.

learn.p: 3 friends share a £12.60 pizza bill equally: £12 ÷ 3 = £4 and 60p ÷ 3 = 20p. Each pays £4.20.

questions.q: 5 stickers cost 30p each. How much is that in pence?
3 bus tickets cost £1.75 each. What is the total in pounds?
4 friends share £10 equally. How much does each get, in pounds?
A box of 6 doughnuts costs £3.60. How much is one doughnut in pence?
You save £1.50 every week. How many pounds will you have after 8 weeks?
10 packs of cards cost £24.90. How much is one pack in pounds?
questions.hint: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right.

units.title: Best buys and budgets
units.blurb: Which is the better deal? Can you afford it?

learn.p: Pack A: 4 rolls for £2. Pack B: 6 rolls for £2.70. One roll in A costs 200p ÷ 4 = 50p. One roll in B costs 270p ÷ 6 = 45p. B is the better buy.
Or compare the same amount: 12 rolls would be 3 packs of A (£6) or 2 packs of B (£5.40). B is cheaper again.
A budget is the most you can spend. If you have £10, add up the prices as you go and stop before you go over.

questions.q: Which is the better buy? 2 pens for £1.20 or 5 pens for £2.50?
options: They cost the same per pen
questions.hint: Find the price of one pen in each pack.
questions.explain: 120p ÷ 2 = 60p per pen. 250p ÷ 5 = 50p per pen. So 5 for £2.50 is better.

questions.q: Which is the better buy? 3 bananas for 90p or 4 bananas for £1.00?
options: They cost the same per banana

questions.q: You have £10. Which shopping can you afford? Paint £4.50, brushes £3.75, paper £2.40.
options: Paint, brushes and two packs of paper
questions.hint: Add up each choice and compare with £10.
questions.explain: Paint + brushes = £8.25, under £10. All three = £10.65, which is over budget.

questions.q: A school trip costs £18. Amy has saved £11.50. How much more does she need, in pounds?
A cafe offers 3 cookies for the price of 2. Cookies are 80p each. How much do you pay for 3, in pence?
A £20 jumper is in a sale with £5 off. What is the sale price?
